What it actually does is define an HTTP query-string contract for inventory.controller.ts, which is an infrastructure file. Three things make it a transport concern. First, `@ApiPropertyOptional` from @nestjs/swagger adds OpenAPI documentation (example, minimum, description), which is HTTP transport documentation. Second, `@Type(() => Number)` from class-transformer turns the raw query-string value into a number, which is request-parsing logic. Third, the class models query parameters for a specific HTTP endpoint, and the folder name `primary-adapters` says the same thing. All of this belongs to the infrastructure (primary/driving adapter) layer, not to a framework-independent application input contract. This is a borderline case: validation DTOs often sit in the application layer. But Swagger annotations and query-string coercion are transport responsibilities, so the file's job does not match its declared layer.
